name: PT Dian Swastatika Sentosa Tbk

frontmatter.title: DSSA: the parts, the upstream and the premium
frontmatter.summary: DSSA is a Sinar Mas conglomerate whose coal arm sits in a separately listed subsidiary. The parts are worth Rp241; the price is 3.1x that value. The konglo lens keeps only part of the premium over twelve months, giving a target of Rp488 and a SELL. The subsidiary's dividends reach the parent; the parent hoards them.
thesis: The parts — the listed coal stake at the covered subsidiary's house target, the non-coal segments at audited net book, the unallocated remainder, net of non-controlling interests and less a holding-company discount — are worth Rp241 after twelve months, far below the Rp675 price.
The own-history P/E and P/BV are dropped, not down-weighted: they are struck on the price history OJK found manipulated and sit several times above the parts.

The upstream is real: the parent receives its controlling share of the coal subsidiary's distributions. What never happens is a distribution from DSSA to its own shareholders, so the discount is a hoarding discount, not a dead channel.
Power and technology are fallback book marks, not house-card valuations; the report tests them and shows what a book haircut is worth.

PT SMT, which we infer is the controlling shareholder, has been fined over manipulation of trading in DSSA's own shares and the related parties have now paid the penalties; the konglo lens slows the premium's compression rather than removing it.

catalysts.event: OJK hands the sanction letters over in person to PT SMT (inferred to be the controlling shareholder) and to nine exchange members
The regulator describes its market-conduct sanctions as the largest in its history and keeps criminal escalation open
OJK confirms the administrative fines in the DSSA, BREN and CUAN cases have been paid in full to the state treasury by the related parties, not the issuers
HSC names leave the IHSG calculation; DSSA is on the list
IDX minimum free-float step takes effect for large caps; DSSA's free float clears the raised minimum but the group remains in the HSC regime
MSCI consultation on moving Indonesia to Standalone status closes, with a decision due by 30 June 2027

blocks.text: **This update records the settlement of the OJK penalty and two corrections; the rating stays SELL and the target moves to Rp488 from the prior published level.** The move comes from the GEMS October interim dividend now carried as a bridge item and from restoring three FY2026 earnings drivers to the last actual, not from any change in the parts [S25, S0, S9]. On 30 October the regulator confirmed that the related parties behind the DSSA, BREN and CUAN cases have paid the administrative fines in full and that the money has been deposited to the state treasury: IDR2.10tn across the three, of which the DSSA-related share is IDR1.50tn [S21]. It stressed that the payers are the parties, not the listed issuers [S21], and that the DSSA-case sanction is attributed to DSSA while the Kompas and Antara reports name the recipient as PT SMT, a subsidiary, so the obligation sat below the listed parent and has been discharged by the parties; no residual claim on DSSA's equity remains [S10, S14, S21]. No line in the parts moves; the konglo lens already carries the enforcement finding as a regime flag, and that flag stays. What the event does change is the read on the file: the administrative leg is settled, removing the tail of a contested or unpaid penalty, but the regulator describes the DSSA conduct as a criminal market-manipulation act that lifted the share price and continues to summon 12 securities-firm directors alongside individual and foreign corporate parties [S21, S13]. The criminal file and the governance discount therefore remain, and the rating and target are unchanged. The next three paragraphs restate the view the update carries forward.

**The view carried into this update removes the OJK-tainted multiples and corrects the upstream claim; the house maintains SELL and the Rp488 target.** The change from the prior published level within this revision is the interim bridge and the restored FY2026 drivers described above. The fundamental now rests entirely on the parts: the coal stake at the covered subsidiary's house target, the non-coal businesses at audited segment net book, plus the unallocated corporate remainder, net of the non-controlling interests that belong to outside holders and less a holding-company discount. That is Rp241 a share after twelve months, or Rp216 today [S0]. The price is Rp675, or 3.1x fundamental value [S0]. The konglo lens keeps part of that premium because a float of 21.5% sets the marginal price: the controller holds 59.9%, treasury holds 19.7% and the rest is public, so the base regime case closes 45% of the log gap for Rp453, and probability-weighted across the three regime scenarios the target is Rp488, a -27.6% total return [S0]. The rating is SELL.

**Three corrections.** First, the own-history P/E and P/BV are dropped, not cut to a token weight: they are struck on the tape the regulator found was planned, structured and price-lifted [S10, S13, S14], and because they sat several times above the parts, even a ten per cent weight supplied about half the old fundamental. Second, the parent has received subsidiary dividends: the cash flow records the outside shareholders' share at USD 105m in FY2025 and USD 237m in FY2024 [S9], and the subsidiary's note records a total FY2024 distribution of USD 500m to all shareholders [S9]; at the 51.0% stake, the controlling share reaches DSSA and is reinvested. Third, the card's holdco deductions are applied: overhead capitalised at ten times the sourced office line, and a tested parent net-debt position [S9, F62].

**The variant view.** The market is not paying for the coal arm, which sits in a separately listed subsidiary valued at a fraction of the parent, nor for the non-coal parts at audited book. It is paying a 3.1x premium to the whole. The konglo lens explains why that premium can persist — thin float, index deletions and a live sanction — but it does not make the premium value. We mark the subsidiary at its house target, below its own quote, so the parts are not flattered by the market's optimism about the child [S0]. The nearest bull catalyst is not a first upstream from the subsidiary, which already happens, but a first distribution from DSSA to its own shareholders.

DSSA reports in US dollars and describes itself as an energy and infrastructure company [S9]. Revenue comes from four segments — captive steam and electricity, fertilizer and chemicals trading, coal mining and trading, and cable television, internet and technology, plus small renewable and other lines [S9].

Coal dominates: mining and trading revenue was 2,488 USD m against group revenue of 2,791.2 [S9, S0]; the audited segment note puts mining at almost nine-tenths of revenue [S9]. The coal business sits in PT Golden Energy Mines Tbk, listed since 2011, in which DSSA holds 51.0% directly [S9, S3]. The mines operate under coal contracts of work (CCoW), whose royalty and permit terms the group flags as a margin risk [S9]. The minority interest of 444.4 is largely the coal subsidiary's outside owners [S9].

The other pillars are smaller. Technology revenue was 212 USD m last year and 170 USD m in the first half, roughly double the prior period [S9, S6]; fertilizer and chemicals was 90.9 USD m; power has no external revenue because the fee is earned inside the group [S9]. The group says the energy pillar funds the build-out of the others, its stated reason for not paying a dividend [S6, S9].

Ownership is concentrated: PT Sinar Mas Tunggal holds 59.9% of issued shares, treasury stock is 19.7% and the remaining 21.5% is public float [S9, S0]. The account groups public and treasury together [S9]; treasury is not additive to the controller block, and the three disclosed slices do not sum to a hundred because the free-float measure uses a different base from the share register. The entity the regulator has just sanctioned is named in the sources only as PT SMT [S10, S14]; we infer it is the controlling shareholder PT Sinar Mas Tunggal, an inference no source confirms. Market capitalisation is IDR104,444,183,193.75tn with about IDR424,795,647.18tn traded a day, so no liquidity discount applies [S0]; the fifty-two week range of 432.0 to 4,640.0 shows the repricing [S0].

A listed parent that owns stakes in separately listed children usually trades at a discount to what
those stakes are worth: minority holders cannot direct the cash, cannot force a distribution, and bear
the cost of whatever the parent builds next. The discount narrows only when something specific and
dated forces value up to the parent.

DSSA is five businesses, and the house card says mark each on its own terms rather than apply a blanket multiple to the group [S9]. The largest is thermal coal. The coal price reaches DSSA through the listed subsidiary's own quote and house target, not through a mine model we build here, so the coal path enters the parts as the market's and the subsidiary's own view rather than a second, independent forecast [S9, S12].

Power is a captive processing fee with a large asset base and no external revenue [S9]. Chemicals is a low-margin distribution book [S9]. Digital infrastructure — broadband, homepasses and a data-centre build — is the fastest-growing revenue line [S6, S9]. Competitively, the group is a follower: the coal producer is mid-curve with a wide calorific range and a domestic, China and India customer mix [S9]; broadband and data centres face far larger incumbents in a scale business with front-loaded capital [S6, S9]; chemicals is a price-taker [S9]. Only the power processing agreement has a semblance of a moat, and it is the part with the largest book and the least external revenue [S9].

Two external influences matter: the market-conduct file against the controlling shareholder — whose administrative fines the related parties have now paid, while the criminal file stays open — which the house framework reads as a manipulation-class flag [S10, S14, S21], and the coal royalty and permit regime, which the group flags as a margin risk [S9] and which reaches our target through the subsidiary's model.

Revenue fell to 2,791.2 last year from 3,017.8, and gross margin compressed to 33.7% from 40.7% [S0]. Net profit to the parent was 230.5, of which minorities took 130.7 [S0, S9], and return on equity was 16.0% [S9].

The data pack's depreciation is a fraction of the real charge because the cash-flow statement uses the direct method and carries no add-back; the segment note discloses consolidated D&A of 78.2 USD m and 83.6 USD m for the last two years, and the model carries that restated charge [S9]. Two splits make older per-share metrics not like-for-like [S0].

The forecast reproduces the last audited year's economics: the other non-operating line (44.2) and the minority split (130.7) are carried at the FY2025A actual, not the engine's three-year default, and the cost of debt is the FY2025 effective rate [S0, S9]. Revenue growth of 10.0% takes the top line to 3,070.3, on the two plan numbers the company has disclosed: first-half technology revenue roughly doubled [S6, F20], and the coal subsidiary guides 58 Mt of sales against the 55.0 Mt it itself reports for 2025 [S12, F48, F79], about five and a half per cent higher, while DSSA's consolidated coal sales were 56.7 Mt [S9, F1]. Gross margin of 33.7% and EBITDA margin of 17.2% are held at last year's levels because no source supports a squeeze or a recovery [S0, S9], giving EBITDA of 527.0 and net profit to the parent of 212.1 [S0]. **Reconciling the first half.** The first half ran at roughly a third higher group revenue, with coal up nearly thirty per cent and technology up nearly ninety per cent [S6]; we do not extrapolate that run-rate because it is struck against a weak prior-year half and a coal-price run-rate the company's own volume plan does not repeat. The full-year forecast instead applies the subsidiary's own volume plan (about five and a half per cent higher, above) and holds margins at last year's level; that combination is the most likely path, not a cautious one, and it is why FY2026E growth sits below the first-half actual. FY2026E parent profit of 212.1 is now above the reported first half's share of it and below FY2025A only because interest income falls with the year-end cash balance and interest expense rises on the larger debt carried in FY2025 — both mechanical and sourced, not a haircut [S0, S9, S6]. Beyond FY2026E the revenue path is a hand-set fade that feeds only the zero-weighted earnings cross-checks and does not reach the target, which is the sum of the parts [S0, S9].

Capex of 513.7 against EBITDA of 527.0 leaves free cash flow to the firm of 38.6, and the same comparison was negative last year at -99.4 [S0]: spending absorbs essentially all the businesses generate, concentrated in the non-coal pillars [S9, S6]. The FCFF bridge is EBITDA, less cash tax and capex, plus a working-capital release: operating working capital falls from 610.8 to 478.9 as revenue growth outruns the last year's build, a release of {{fin.FY2026E.delta_nwc|abs|money}} that is shown here rather than buried in the net figure [S0]. We hold capex at last year's ratio without a source to change it [S0, S9].

The balance sheet carries cash of 575.5, debt of 1,486.2 and minorities of 444.4, for net debt of 910.6 and net debt to EBITDA of 1.9 [S0]. This is not charged twice: each part is valued after its own liabilities [S9]. The parent's bonds are inside the segment marks — segment liabilities of 2,121 USD m are within two per cent of consolidated liabilities (assets of 4,415 USD m less equity of 2,261 USD m) — so netting them again would double-count [S9]. The guarantees are a contingent claim in section six [S9].

**Earnings quality.** Accruals are negative in two of the last three years and marginally positive in the third: operating cash was 330 USD m, 693 USD m and 1,031 USD m against net profit of 361.2, 542.8 and 865.3 [S0, S9]. Cash covered profit in two of the three years and fell short by a whisker in the third, well inside the threshold. Free cash flow to the firm turns negative — -99.4, -139.4, 307.6 [S0] — a capital-spending story, not an accruals one. Technology assets grew from 1,162 USD m to 2,208 USD m in a year [S9]. The regulatory action is not a listing-status action on the issuer, and the penalties are borne, and now paid, by the related parties rather than the issuer [S10, S14, S21]. One sanctioned member is PT SS, whose director received an underwriter-licence freeze [S14, F57]; no DSSA entity or director is among the sanctioned parties [S14].

Related-party purchases were 0.4% of cost of revenues and the related-party slice of G&A was 0.9%, mainly family property, telecom and insurance entities [S9]. The larger exposure is structural: allocating a data centre or broadband network between listed and unlisted vehicles is the family's choice [S9, S6], and the data-centre build already runs through a related party — KMG bought the package for the group's data-centre project from PT LG Sinarmas Technology Solutions for Rp1.2tn [S9, F67].

**PSAK 16.** The power book does not carry a revaluation surplus today: the plants were sold in 2024, the decrease in the surplus was 160 USD m, the cumulative increment transferred to retained earnings was USD 111m, and the surplus line is nil [S9]. **Structure flags**: two splits, the restructuring that moved the subsidiary stake onto the parent's books, the elimination column of -1,954 USD m, and the treasury block of 1,516 million shares, 19.7% of issued capital [S9]. The disclosure items are optics-class; the regulator's finding that trading in DSSA's shares was planned, structured and price-lifting is manipulation-class, and it sits at the controlling shareholder rather than in the issuer's accounts [S10, S13, S14].

The house card values a holding company on its parts, less holdco net debt and a discount the base rate says persists [S0]. The parts carry 100% of the blend: the own-history P/E and P/BV are dropped because both sat several times above the parts and are struck on the tape OJK found manipulated [S0, S10, S13, S14]. The cost of equity is 12.6% and the weighted average cost of capital 10.8%, built in the table [S0].

**The parts.** Each mark is a listed price or an audited segment book; the bridge reconciles to consolidated equity and then cuts the consolidated total back to the parent's share. The coal stake is at the covered subsidiary's house target, not its quote, because the konglo card marks a covered listed subsidiary at its house target and that target sits below the market price. The house target and the quote come from GEMS.JK's own covered report and model, the subsidiary rated HOLD with its house target below its quote [S20].

| Part | Mark | | --- | --- | | PT Golden Energy Mines Tbk, 51.0% stake | house target [S20] | | Steam and electricity | net book, fallback [S9] | | Cable TV, internet and technology | net book, fallback [S9] | | Fertilizer and chemicals | net book [S9] | | Renewable energy | net book [S9] | | Other | net book [S9] | | Intra-group elimination | deduction [S9] | | Unallocated corporate and tax remainder | value [S9] | | Non-controlling interests | deduction [S9] |

Marks are assets less liabilities: 2,659 USD m less 668 USD m, 2,208 USD m less 1,114 USD m, 57.4 USD m less 32.6 USD m, 75.2 USD m less 1.0 USD m, 37.6 USD m less 0.6 USD m, the elimination -1,954 USD m less -197 USD m, and the remainder equity 2,261 USD m less segment net assets [S9].

**Power and technology are fallbacks, and tested.** Power has no external revenue and no segment result; its FY2024 comparative result was -0.2 [S9], so a fee business with no disclosed profit is at net book rather than an invented multiple. Technology has a segment result of 142 USD m, before operating expense; against net book of 2,208 USD m less 1,114 USD m that is about an eighth of book, and after the FY2024 comparative operating expense of USD 78.6m it is a mid-single-digit return, which does not prove the book [S9]. We keep net book at par as the most likely mark, not as caution: no house card exists for these unlisted segments, audited segment net book is the only disclosed measure of their capital, and the technology result shows a positive, if thin, return on it. A ten per cent haircut is the bear's mark and a re-rating on a future segment-return disclosure is the bull's; the book is a floor with a range [S0, S9]. The PSAK 16 objection is answered: the plants were sold, the cumulative increment was transferred to retained earnings, and the surplus line is nil [S9, F49, F76].

**The reconciliation.** The segment books are stated in full, so the parts must be cut back to the parent's share. Consolidated equity is 2,261 USD m [S9], of which total non-controlling interests are 444 USD m [S9] and the coal subsidiary 350 USD m [S9]. The coal segment's net book — 1,051 USD m less 502 USD m — is replaced by the parent's 51.0% share of the GEMS house target; because GEMS's own net assets (implied by the 350 USD m NCI at the minority share) exceed that segment book, the deduction is the total NCI less the coal book the GEMS mark already removes beyond the parent's share. The bridge is equity less that deduction plus the GEMS mark over the coal net book [S9]; the elimination is already inside consolidated equity, so there is no second elimination, and the remainder is positive [S9].

**Why audited book, not the first-half equity.** The SOTP starts from the audited FY2025 segment books, not the higher first-half-2026 consolidated equity [S6]. The segment marks are audited and the half-year uplift sits largely in the coal column, which the GEMS house mark already replaces at the subsidiary's own value; reading the increase straight into the parent's equity would count that uplift twice. The choice is disclosed, and it is why the valuation does not rise with the first-half equity.

**The holdco bridge.** The parent's bonds and sukuk are inside segment liabilities — segment liabilities of 2,121 USD m are within two per cent of consolidated liabilities, and the Phase IV issue alone was Rp0.3tn of bonds plus Rp1.2tn of sukuk [S9, F68, F69] — so netting them again would double-count. What is not in the marks is parent overhead: the parent-level office expense of USD 3.9m [S9, F62], capitalised at ten times, is the deduction, a floor because the parent-only share of salaries is not published. The guarantees are a contingent claim in section six [S9, F63-F66].

**The upstream, corrected.** The old report said the parent had never received a dividend; that was wrong. The cash flow records NCI dividends of USD 105m in FY2025 and USD 237m in FY2024 [S9], and the subsidiary's note records total distributions of USD 500m for FY2024 and USD 500m for FY2023 to all holders [S9]. At 51.0% the parent receives the controlling share; it covers the capitalised office cost about six and a half times on FY2024 and almost three times on FY2025 [S9, F58-F62]. The flow has continued inside the valuation window: GEMS paid a US$200.0m FY2026 interim on 22 October 2026, after the 30 June balance sheet, of which DSSA's 51.0% is about 132m equivalent — carried as a bridge item and leaving the parent's pro-forma net debt lower by that amount [S25, F88]. The discount is a hoarding discount — cash arrives and is not passed on — not a dead channel.

**The discount.** A discount of twenty to forty per cent persists indefinitely, and a narrower discount needs a dated catalyst that upstreams cash [S0]. The one precedent is stale: a 2023 buyback took 484 USD m of stock off the market, of which 1,516 million shares, 19.7% of issued capital, still sits in treasury; part was reissued in 2024 for 48.9 USD m [S9]. The policy permits up to 30.0% of net profit and the parent has never paid a dividend [S9, S0]. We charge 30%, the middle of the persistent band, on the base rate and the non-enforcement structure — the related-party flow, the treasury overhang and the cross-guarantees [S9, F46-F67]; the stale buyback argues against the wide end, that structure against the tight end. The OJK trading sanction is not a second discount: the konglo card assigns it to the lens, and it is counted there once [S10, S14]. Even the tight end leaves the parts below the price [S0].

The sum of the parts is Rp216 a share; grown at the cost of equity for a year, with no dividend leg, that is the fundamental value of Rp241 [S0]. The price is Rp675, so the gap is the premium ratio of 3.1x, not the final target's expected return; the -27.6% figure is the return to the lens target only [S0].

**The konglo lens.** The engine measures the log premium of 1.1 [S0] and assumes only a share closes in twelve months because the marginal price is set by float: 21.5% of the capital trades [S9, S0]. The closing share is slowed by HSC listing, exit from the IHSG and the index family, and the live sanction [S15, S16, S10, S14], and is run over three regime scenarios, weighted (base at 50%): **bear** closes 85% of the gap for Rp287; **base** closes 45% for Rp453; **bull** closes none and the premium holds for Rp760 [S0]. Probability-weighted, the target is Rp488. We do not shade the parts toward or away from the market price [S0].

**What the price implies.** The engine's reverse DCF cannot solve the price inside the discount range: it searches for the holdco discount that would reproduce the Rp675 price from the parts, and the price sits above the undiscounted parts, so no positive discount brackets it [S0]. We disclose the implication directly instead. The parts are worth Rp216 a share after the 30% discount, and even at a zero discount they would be worth only the undiscounted marked value; the price is above that, so the market is paying a premium to the marked parts, not a discount [S0, S20]. The reverse-DCF answer is therefore a negative discount — a premium — and the konglo lens, not the DCF, is what keeps part of it. The same reading applies to the cross-checks: at the current FY2025A multiples of 25.0x earnings and 3.2x book [S0] the quoted price already assumes a re-rating the parts do not support, which is why the own-history P/E and P/BV are dropped rather than blended. Dropping them is the largest single choice in the target, and it is made because they are struck on the tape the regulator found manipulated [S10, S13, S14]; the peer set the house uses for holdcos (ADRO, BRPT, CUAN, FOLK and TOBA at the same discount, ASII a little tighter) supports the discount itself, not a multiple-of-earnings mark for this name [S0, S9].

**Look-through earnings and leverage.** DSSA's look-through earnings are 131.7m, the 51.0% share of the coal subsidiary's FY2025A parent profit, against reported parent profit of 230.5 [S20, S0]: the coal arm is the earnings engine and the parent's other parts contribute little. Look-through leverage is low — the subsidiary carries net debt of 22.3m on equity of 702.5m [S20] — so the parent's value is not a levered bet on the coal price; it is a cash-generative asset sitting behind a holding-company structure. On the discount itself, the record holds no archived five-year series of price against marked parts (the name has been reclassified and split twice, and no historical SOTP exists), so the 30% is anchored on the house holdco base rate and the peer discounts above, not on a five-year mean we cannot strike [S0]. The current discount to the parts is a premium, at the top of nothing in that record.

The grid is driven by the discount and the cost of equity and reports pre-lens values; it does not bracket the target because the lens adds most of the distance to the price, and it does not bracket the share price because the price requires a negative discount [S0]. The reverse-DCF implication above and the konglo lens are the two legs that reach it. Section five shows the subsidiary's bear target effect instead.

**Currency.** The model translates a USD-reporting group into rupiah at the spot rate, while the house macro deck carries a slightly weaker FY2027E rate [S0]. The difference is about one per cent and moves the target one-for-one; we disclose it rather than blend two FX paths, because the business earns in dollars and the rupiah target is a translation, not a forecast of the exchange rate [S0].

On this method the target is set by the marked parts and the discount; the largest part is the subsidiary's house value, imported from its own model, so the grid shocks the discount and the two scenarios are discount scenarios in form [S0]. **Bear**: the governance file escalates, nothing is returned to DSSA holders, the coal marker normalises and the digital build consumes capital. The subsidiary already publishes a bear target; at that target the controlling stake is worth less than half its base mark, and the parent's fundamental value falls by about a quarter, while the lens cushions the twelve-month target [S0]. A ten per cent haircut to the two fallback book marks has a similar order of effect. Two structure tails sit outside every mark. First, the cross-guarantee stack: DSSA guarantees EMR facilities of Rp3.6tn, Rp0.4tn and Rp2.0tn and the PT SMPlus data-centre facility of Rp0.4tn [S9, F63-F66]. These are facility plafon, not drawn balances — the accounts do not split drawn from undrawn — so a call on the full stack is about a seventh of the gross parts and would wipe out the capitalised parent overhead many times over; it is sized as a bear tail on the maximum, not netted in the base, and the undrawn share is disclosed as unknown rather than assumed away [S9]. Second, dilution: the annual report's funding waterfall runs internal cash, then short-term debt, then long-term debt, then new shares [S9]; we found no announced rights issue or placement in the sources reviewed, a checked absence rather than proof [S9]. A discounted placement against a controlled price is the classic per-share leak in this structure. **Bull**: a dated capital-allocation signal — the GEMS FY2026 final dividend payable by 30 June 2027 upstreaming to DSSA, a repeat buyback, a first distribution to DSSA holders or a stake sale — narrows the discount, with the 58Mt plan delivered and technology already doubling [S6, S9, S12, S20]: a value of Rp247 and a target of Rp278, with base at 45% [S0]. The KMG-LG Sinarmas data-centre package (Rp1.2tn, F67) is not valued separately: it is already inside the KMG segment's book and the group discloses no project return, so a project value would be invented; the bull credits only the operating leverage it gives the technology line [S9, F67]. Even at the subsidiary's own bull target the parent's lens target stays below the price: the largest component is a covered subsidiary's house target the parent does not control [S9].

**The konglo regime scenarios.** The lens reads the price at 3.1x fundamental value and asks how much of the 1.1 log gap the regime lets close [S0]. DSSA is on the HSC list and out of the IHSG from 2 November 2026 [S15, S16]; it was deleted from the MSCI Global Standard and FTSE Large Cap indexes in 2026 [S17, S18]; and the controlling shareholder carries an OJK sanction whose administrative fines the related parties have now paid, with criminal escalation still open [S10, S13, S14, S21]. The free float of 21.5% clears the raised fifteen per cent minimum, so no forced supply step sits in the window [S0, S19]. The dated catalysts are the MSCI Standalone consultation, feedback closing on 30 April 2027 with a decision by 30 June 2027 [S22], the IDX free-float deadlines from 31 March 2027 [S24], and the enforcement file [S13]. The bear case is that the premium the lens keeps is what the 2026 regime is dismantling, so a faster unravel is a real risk.

Five risks carry weight. **Governance (high likelihood, high impact)**: the controlling shareholder has been fined over manipulation of DSSA's shares, the related parties have paid the administrative penalties in full, exchange members were sanctioned, and criminal escalation stays open [S14, S10, S13, S21]; we read it as a regime factor the konglo lens carries [S0]. **Capital allocation (high likelihood, high impact)**: capex absorbs essentially all of group EBITDA, the parent receives the subsidiary's distributions but passes none to its shareholders, and the equity has no yield support [S0, S9]. **Coal-market (medium likelihood, medium impact)**: the coal stake is marked at the subsidiary's house target, so a lower coal marker lowers the largest part directly [S9]. **Disclosure (high likelihood, medium impact)**: no segmental operating profit is published for the largest book-value segments; a technology-profit disclosure would be the biggest positive change [S9]. **Currency (medium likelihood, medium impact)**: the group reports in dollars, so the rupiah value of the parts moves with the exchange rate while the businesses do not [S0].
A dated action that distributes cash to DSSA's own shareholders — a dividend, buyback or stake sale — would justify a narrower discount [S9], while a criminal escalation widens it [S13, S10].

**The konglo profile.** DSSA is the Sinar Mas group's energy and infrastructure holding, the Widjaja family's listed vehicle and the parent of the separately listed coal miner [S9]. The controlling holding company holds 59.9% and insider holdings are 66.3%, leaving a free float of 21.5% [S9, S0]. That float clears the raised fifteen per cent minimum [S0, S19], but DSSA is on the HSC list and out of the IHSG from 2 November 2026 [S15, S16], and was deleted from the MSCI Global Standard and FTSE Large Cap indexes in 2026 [S17, S18]. The live enforcement item is the OJK manipulation sanction against PT SMT (inferred to be the controlling shareholder), the largest in the regulator's history: the related parties have paid the administrative fines — IDR2.10tn across the three cases, the DSSA-related share IDR1.50tn — while the criminal file stays open [S10, S13, S14, S21]. The marginal price is set by the public float — about a fifth of the capital — not by the whole register, and the controller plus treasury hold the rest [S9, S0].

**Structure flags.** Cross-guarantees: DSSA guarantees EMR facilities of Rp3.6tn, Rp0.4tn and Rp2.0tn and the PT SMPlus data-centre facility of Rp0.4tn [S9, F63-F66], contingent claims disclosed and not netted in the parts. These are facility plafon, not drawn balances: the accounts disclose the maximum guaranteed amount and do not split drawn from undrawn, so the bear tail uses the full stack and the report says so rather than presenting it as an outstanding claim [S9]. Treasury: the 2023 buyback left 1,516 million shares, or 19.7% of issued capital, in treasury [S9, F46, F47] — potential supply and a governance overhang. Pledges: the report discloses pledges of GEMS-group shares and receivables for the subsidiary's bank facilities [S9, F74]; we found no disclosure of a pledge of the controlling shareholder's DSSA stake, a checked absence, not proof. Dilution: the stated funding waterfall runs internal cash, then short-term debt, then long-term debt, then new shares [S9]; no rights issue or placement is announced in the sources reviewed, but the channel is live [S9]. Related-party assets: the data-centre build runs through PT LG Sinarmas Technology Solutions at Rp1.2tn [S9, F67], and allocating assets between listed and unlisted vehicles is the family's choice [S9]. Related-party land moves both ways: on 29 October 2026 BSDE unit Surya Inter Wisesa signed a PPJB to sell 16.6 ha in the D-Hub SEZ at BSD City to DSSA unit SMPlus Cakrawala Cipta Gemilang, with the consideration not disclosed [S23, F89], and the FY2025 accounts record the 6 February 2025 related-party purchase of land by KMG, a subsidiary, from BSDE, also without a disclosed value in the events calendar [S9]. Neither is in the parts: no consideration, valuation or NCI effect is disclosed, so a mark would be invented. Each widens the warranted discount.

**Ownership and the sanction.** Minority holders have no practical influence over board composition or the decision to reinvest [S9]. The authority imposed an administrative fine of 1.5 Rp trn on the PT SMT (inferred to be the controlling shareholder) over manipulation of DSSA's shares, found the manipulation planned and structured and price-lifting, sanctioned 9 exchange members and warned eight sales staff, and handed the letters over on 21 October [S10, S14]. On 30 October it confirmed that the related parties, not the issuers, have paid the fines in full and that the money is in the state treasury: IDR2.10tn across the three cases, the DSSA-related share IDR1.50tn [S21]. It will escalate to a criminal investigation if the evidence supports one, calls the DSSA conduct a criminal market-manipulation act and the sanction the largest in its history, and continues to summon 12 securities-firm directors plus individual and foreign corporate parties [S13, S21]. On the house framework this is a manipulation-class flag; the konglo card routes it to the regime lens, so it slows the premium's compression there and is not counted a second time in the holdco discount [S10, S11, S13, S14].

**Dividend and ESG.** The policy permits up to 30.0% of net profit [S9] and the parent has paid none to its own shareholders, on the company's stated explanation that its subsidiaries require the capital [S9]. The subsidiary does pay: the cash flow and its dividend note show distributions to all shareholders, of which the parent receives the controlling share [S9, F58-F61]. An upstream that arrives at the parent and stops there is the whole cost of the structure — a hoarding discount — and it is why the dividend-yield method is dropped [S0, S9]. On ESG the exposures are the ordinary ones for Indonesian thermal coal at the subsidiary, plus the governance sanction, on which this name would not pass a controlling-shareholder conduct screen today [S10], and a transition claim resting on disclosure too thin to underwrite [S9, S6].

Only the regulatory file and the index calendar carry dates. The sanction letters were handed over on 21 October to PT SMT (inferred to be the controlling shareholder) and exchange members [S14, S13], and by 30 October the related parties had paid the administrative fines in full [S21]; whether the issuer itself faces action and whether the investigation reaches the courts is what sets the governance discount [S10, S11, S21]. The HSC names leave the IHSG calculation from 2 November 2026 [S16], the IDX free-float step lands on 31 March 2027 [S19], and the MSCI Standalone consultation closes on 30 April 2027 with a decision by 30 June 2027 [S22]. The rest are undated watch items [S9]. The HSC exit on 2 November 2026 and the GEMS FY2026 final dividend, payable by the IDX norm on 30 June 2027, are the two dated items that could move the discount and the upstream respectively [S16, S20].

The monitorables are method-specific. Any distribution from DSSA to its own shareholders — a dividend, buyback or stake sale — would attack the discount directly; the subsidiary's upstream already reaches the parent, so the missing leg is the parent's payout [S9]. Segmental operating profit and capital employed for technology, power and chemicals would let us mark those parts on their own cards instead of at fallback book [S9]. And who pays for the data centre and broadband build, at what return, is the item that would most change the parts valuation [S6, S9].

bear.narrative: Built from the bear drivers, not the discount alone. The coal stake falls to GEMS's own published bear target, where the 51% mark is worth about a third less than the base house mark [S20]; the two fallback book marks (power and technology, together the largest non-coal parts) take a ten per cent haircut as the digital build fails to earn its capital [S9]; the governance file escalates to a criminal investigation and the Rp6.42tn cross-guarantee plafon becomes a live claim, while the holdco discount widens to the wide end of the band at 40% [S9, F63-F66]. The engine's SOTP mark uses the subsidiary's probability-weighted house target and cannot re-price GEMS inside a scenario, so the table's bear leg moves the discount to the wide end and §5 states the GEMS bear mark and the book haircut separately; the probability of the bear is raised to 30% to carry that weight.

bull.narrative: Built from the bull drivers. The coal subsidiary delivers its 58Mt plan and holds the GEMS base house mark [S12, S20]; the GEMS FY2026 final dividend is paid by 30 June 2027 and a first distribution or repeat buyback at DSSA itself finally upstreams cash to the parent's holders [S9, F44]; technology revenue, already roughly doubled in the first half, earns its book and the discount narrows to the tight end of the band at 20% [S6, F20, S9]. Even here the parts do not reach the market's price.

groups.name: Sinar Mas group (Widjaja family)

konglo.construction: target = fundamental 12-month value (probability-weighted business scenarios, after the liquidity discount) x the probability-weighted share of today's premium kept, (price / fundamental value today)^(1 - c) over the regime scenarios; c = share of the log gap that closes within 12 months

assumptions.label: Revenue growth
assumptions.basis: FY2026E is anchored on the two plan numbers that ARE traceable and the last actual. The company's own target table carries revenue targets for FY2025 and FY2024 and gives no 2026 revenue number at all [S9, F15]. What the register DOES give for 2026 is the listed coal subsidiary's own plan — 58Mt of production and sales, above the 54.95Mt the subsidiary itself reports for 2025 [S12, F48, F79] — and the group's first-half technology revenue, roughly doubled year on year to USD 170.49m [S6, F20]. Coal is roughly nine-tenths of group revenue [S9, F7]. A full-year doubling of the USD 211.8m technology line [S9, F38] adds about eight per cent to the group, and the coal volume plan adds about five and a half, which puts FY2026E about a tenth above FY2025A. That is a drift UP from the last actual that rests only on the two sourced plan numbers, not on a coal-price assumption. From FY2027E the first-half technology step is not extrapolated a second time and no source supports volume beyond the 2026 plan, so the top line fades toward the last actual rather than compounding; the fade feeds only the small earnings cross-checks and does not set the target, which is the sum of the parts.

assumptions.label: Gross margin at base input costs
assumptions.basis: Set at the last audited year's own gross margin (consolidated gross profit over revenue, FY2025A [S0, S9]) rather than the three-year average the starter carried, because the most-likely rule is that FY+1 reproduces the last actual year's economics and no source supports a further squeeze. The three-year average is flattered by FY2023, when the coal marker was roughly a third higher than it is today, so carrying it forward would import a peak-year margin into the forecast.

assumptions.label: SG&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: The last audited year's own ratio of SG&A and other operating expense to revenue [S0], held flat in real terms. The group's overhead carries the technology, chemicals and corporate functions as well as the mine, and nothing in the LK sources a step down; a decline would be an unsourced haircut.

assumptions.label: D&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: Set from the LK's OWN depreciation and amortisation, not the data pack's cash-flow feed: the group reports consolidated D&A of USD 78.2m for FY2025 and USD 83.6m for FY2024 in the segment note [F17, F18], roughly three times the pack's direct-method figure, and the ratio of that restated charge to revenue is what the forecast carries. The pack's D&A is small because the IDX cash-flow statement is prepared on the direct method and carries no add-back.

assumptions.label: Capex / revenue
assumptions.basis: The last audited year's own ratio of capital spending to revenue [S0, S9], held flat. The group spends across the mine, the power assets, the broadband network and the data-centre build, and that spending absorbed essentially all of group EBITDA in the recent audited years; the ratio is the witnessed rate, not a target, and no source supports cutting it.

assumptions.label: Operating working capital / revenue
assumptions.basis: engine default: average of FY2023A, FY2024A, FY2025A (div(nwc, revenue))

assumptions.label: Effective tax rate
assumptions.basis: engine default: average of FY2023A, FY2024A, FY2025A (div(tax, pbt))

assumptions.label: Cost of debt (on opening debt)
assumptions.basis: Set at the FY2025A effective rate of 5.87% (interest expense USD 71.37m on opening debt USD 1,216.33m) rather than the three-year average of 6.66%, which carries the FY2023 rate when debt was much smaller. The last actual is the sourced rate on the current debt stack [S0, S9].

assumptions.label: Yield on opening cash
assumptions.basis: engine default: average of FY2023A, FY2024A, FY2025A (div(interest_income, cash[-1]))

assumptions.label: Net new borrowing
assumptions.basis: Held at the engine default (no new borrowing) with the caveat stated in the report rather than a fabricated financing plan: the LK says only that long-term bank borrowings may rise in the next few years to fund new projects and that the group funds capex from internal cash first, then short-term debt, then long-term debt, then new shares [S9], which is not a number we can date. On this method the forecast balance sheet feeds only the small earnings and book cross-checks, not the target, so an unsourced debt schedule would add false precision. Where the modelled cash path runs thin past the forecast horizon the report says so plainly [S9].

assumptions.label: Other non-operating items
assumptions.basis: Held at the FY2025A actual of USD 44.157m rather than the engine's zero default: the last audited year earned a positive other non-operating line and nothing in the FY2025 accounts or the H1-2026 release sources a step to zero. Carrying the last actual is the most-likely rule; zeroing it was an unsourced haircut that depressed FY2026E parent profit below the reported first half [S0, S9].

assumptions.label: Minorities' share of net profit
assumptions.basis: Set at the FY2025A actual ratio of 36.18% (minority interest USD 130.662m on net profit USD 361.20m) rather than the three-year average of 43.33%, which is inflated by FY2023 when the coal subsidiary earned a peak-year profit. The most-likely rule is to reproduce the last audited year's split; the three-year average quietly raised the minority cut by seven points and pushed FY2026E parent profit below the reported H1-2026 actual [S0, S9].

assumptions.label: Dividend payout
assumptions.basis: Zero, and sourced rather than assumed by omission: the group's policy permits a distribution of up to 30% of net profit [F14], but the accounts record no dividend payment in any reported year [S0, S9] and the company states it has not distributed dividends because its subsidiaries require substantial capital expenditure [S9]. A payout we cannot source, on a name that has never paid one, would be a fabricated leg in the blend; the engine therefore drops the yield method entirely.

assumptions.label: Terminal growth (DCF)
assumptions.basis: The primary method is a sum of the parts with a holding-company discount, so no perpetual growth rate reaches the target; this input only frames the cross-checks. It is set at the house's long-run USD inflation assumption, below the house cap for a USD-reporting name, because a coal-heavy conglomerate should not be assigned perpetual real growth.

assumptions.label: Holding-company discount to SOTP
assumptions.basis: Anchored on the house holdco archetype, not on a hope of narrowing: the base rate for holdco and SOTP names is that a discount of 20-40% persists indefinitely, and the recorded case file requires a NAMED, DATED catalyst that actually upstreams cash before a narrower discount can be underwritten. We hold 30%, the middle of that band. The stale end of the evidence argues against the wide end: this name has ONE capital-return precedent on the record — a holdco buyback of 154,105,327 shares in August-September 2023 for USD 483.8m, part of which was reissued to a third party in August 2024 [S9, F44, F45] — but it is three years old, has never been repeated, and the parent has never paid a dividend to its own holders [S0, S9]. The governance file argues against the tight end on its own merits and is NOT the OJK trading sanction: related-party purchases of family property, telecom and insurance, the data-centre package bought from a family affiliate, the treasury overhang and the cross-guarantees [S9, F46-F67] are the discount-widening structure. The OJK manipulation finding is assigned once, to the konglo lens (enforcement_manipulation), per the konglo card, and is not counted again here. The choice within the band is not load-bearing: the parts value is so far below the price that even the tight end leaves the bull leg below the market price.

challenges.challenge: fund record:165 says "the forecast reproduces the last audited year's economics", but fund record Q4 has FY2026E NP parent 164.340 against FY2025A 230.539 and H1-2026 actual 174.4 (S6). The bridge is mechanical: other_nonop 44.157 to 0, interest_income 90.37 to 40.287, interest_expense 71.37 to 98.950, minority 130.662 (36.2%) to 125.634 on a lower NP (43.3%). No source supports any of these step-downs.
challenges.answer: Restored the FY2025A actuals the defaults had stepped down: other non-operating income USD 44.157m, minority share 36.18% (not the three-year 43.33%) and cost of debt 5.87% (not 6.66%) [S0, S9]. FY2026E parent NP is now USD 212.1m, above the reported H1-2026 actual of USD 174.4m; the remaining gap to FY2025A is interest income falling with year-end cash and interest expense rising on the larger FY2025 debt, both mechanical and stated in §3.

challenges.challenge: fund record records the 29 Oct 2026 sale of 16.6 ha at KEK BSD City by BSDE unit Surya Inter Wisesa to DSSA unit SMPlus Cakrawala Cipta Gemilang, and S9 p322 records the 6 Feb 2025 KMG-BSDE land purchase. Both are related-party land dealings inside the group, omitted from §6, which nevertheless states the searches found nothing on related-party assets and NCI.
challenges.answer: Added both related-party land transactions: the 29 Oct 2026 PPJB for 16.6 ha at D-Hub SEZ BSD City (BSDE unit Surya Inter Wisesa to DSSA unit SMPlus Cakrawala Cipta Gemilang, consideration not disclosed; fact F89 [S23]) and the 6 Feb 2025 KMG-BSDE land purchase [S9 p322]. Both are in §6 and post_bs_review with an explicit statement that no consideration, valuation or NCI effect is disclosed; the searched-and-absent sentence is corrected.

challenges.challenge: The frontmatter and §5 date the MSCI Standalone consultation to 2027-04-30 and 2027-06-30 and cite [S6]; fund record contains no consultation dates (prior Q5). The 2026-11-02 HSC/IHSG exit in S15/S16 is missing from the catalyst calendar entirely.
challenges.answer: Re-archived the MSCI consultation press release itself as S22; it carries feedback until 30 April 2027 and the decision on or before 30 June 2027. The frontmatter, §5 and §7 now cite S22, not S6. Added the 2 November 2026 HSC/IHSG exit to the dated catalyst calendar with source S16.

challenges.section: 1. What the company does / 6. Balance sheet
challenges.challenge: S21 says the Rp1.5tn penalty was paid "kepada DSSA", while S10/S14 say "kepada PT SMT" (a subsidiary). fund record:408 asserts "no claim on DSSA's equity" without reconciling the conflict, and S21 also lists 12 directors, 15 individuals and 11 foreign entities in the enforcement action.
challenges.answer: Reconciled on the record: S21 attributes the Rp1.5tn sanction to the DSSA case but states the payers were related parties, not the issuers; S10 and S14 name the recipient as PT SMT, a subsidiary. The obligation therefore sat below the listed parent and has been discharged, so no residual claim on DSSA equity remains. The 12 securities-firm directors, 15 individuals and 11 foreign entities are already stated (F82). Replaced the bare assertion with this reconciliation.

challenges.challenge: S20 and GEMS.JK report/F13 record a USD200m FY2026 interim paid 22 Oct 2026, after the 30 Jun 2026 balance sheet; DSSA's 51% is ~USD102m. The DSSA upstream line uses only FY2024 and FY2025 dividends (facts F58/F59; S9 p481-482), so a paid inflow inside the valuation window is absent.
challenges.answer: Added the GEMS FY2026 interim: USD 200m declared and paid 22 Oct 2026, DSSA 51% about USD 102m (fact F88 [S25]); carried as a valuation bridge item (value 102.0, probability 1.0), stated in §4 upstream and in post_bs_review. The GEMS house mark is already ex-interim, so this is counted once; pro-forma parent net debt is lower by the receipt.

challenges.challenge: The scenario table moves only holdco_discount by +/-10pp (fund record), giving bear tp 200 and bull 267, yet the report itself says the GEMS bear target implies a parent value down about a quarter, and the bear narrative adds book haircut and guarantee risk. Doubling the bear probability barely moves the blend because the bear is not built from the bear drivers.
challenges.answer: Bear rebuilt from the drivers in narrative and probability: GEMS published bear target on the coal stake, a 10% haircut to the power/technology book marks, the Rp6.42tn guarantee plafon live and the discount at the wide 40% end; bull from the GEMS base mark, the GEMS FY2026 final dividend by 30 June 2027 and a first DSSA distribution, with the discount at 20%. Probabilities are now 30/45/25 so the bear carries weight. The engine scenario lever remains the discount because SOTP holdings cannot be shocked inside a scenario; the bear and bull narratives state the GEMS and book legs separately rather than pretending the table re-prices the subsidiary.

challenges.challenge: The holdco card requires a reverse DCF; fund record records reverse_dcf available false ("price not bracketed") and the sensitivity grid spans 198-269, so neither the 518 target nor the 750 price is inside the tested range. The reader cannot see what price implies.
challenges.answer: The reverse DCF cannot bracket the price: it solves for a holdco discount that reproduces the price, and the price sits above even the undiscounted parts. §4 now discloses this directly and reads the implication as a negative discount (a premium to marked parts), which is the reverse-DCF answer at the boundary; the konglo lens is the leg that keeps part of it. The pre-lens sensitivity grid is labelled as such.

challenges.challenge: The holdco card asks for look-through earnings and leverage and the current discount against the company's own 5-year range. Neither appears: the report gives a static 30% discount and a 1.12412 lens multiplier, with no parent-level earnings yield, look-through net debt/EBITDA, or discount history.
challenges.answer: Added look-through earnings (51% of GEMS FY2025A parent NP = USD 131.7m, fact F85) against DSSA parent profit, and look-through leverage (GEMS net debt USD 22.3m on equity USD 702.5m, facts F86/F87) [S20]. No archived five-year price-to-parts series exists, so the 30% is anchored on the house holdco base rate and peer discounts, and the report says the series is absent rather than inventing one.

challenges.challenge: fund record sets sotp weight 1.0 and pe/pbv 0. The dropped cross-checks resolve to roughly Rp513 (18.98x own-history P/E on FY2025A NP) and Rp860 (4.04x P/BV), and a default 60/25/15 blend to ~Rp382, all above the Rp208 SOTP. The weighting choice, the largest single driver of the target, is not disclosed or defended.
challenges.answer: §4 now discloses why the multiples are dropped and what they imply: at the quoted FY2025A P/E and P/BV the price already assumes a re-rating the parts do not support; the own-history means are below todays quote and several times above the SOTP; the peer holdcos (ADRO, BRPT, CUAN, FOLK, TOBA at the same discount, ASII tighter) support the discount, not an earnings multiple. SOTP carries 100% because the multiples are struck on the OJK-identified manipulated tape [S10, S13, S14], and the choice is disclosed as the largest in the target.

challenges.challenge: The bull case is only a -10pp discount (v0 237, tp 267) with undated catalysts, and it ignores the H1-2026 NP +79.6% and technology revenue +95.6% (S6). No upside from the KMG-LG Sinarmas data-centre project (F67, S9 p608) is valued.
challenges.answer: Bull now carries a dated catalyst: the GEMS FY2026 final dividend payable by the IDX norm on 30 June 2027, upstreaming to DSSA, plus a first DSSA distribution or repeat buyback. The KMG-LG Sinarmas data-centre package is explicitly excluded from the marks with the reason: it is already inside the KMG segment book and no project return is disclosed, so a separate value would be invented.

challenges.challenge: fund record:73 says "a float of 21.46% and a locked controlling-plus-treasury block", but 59.9% + 19.68% + 21.46% exceeds 100%; fund record:398 says "a few per cent of the capital" sets the marginal price against a 21.5% free float. facts F46/F47 quote 1,516.2m treasury shares and 19.68% pre-1:25 (now 37.9bn post-split).
challenges.answer: Ownership arithmetic reconciled: controller 59.90% [S9], treasury 19.68% [F47], and the 21.46% free float is measured on a different base; the annual report groups public and treasury at 40.10% [S9]. Treasury is no longer presented as additive to the controller block, and the marginal-price language now says the public float (about a fifth) sets the price.

challenges.challenge: fund record:117 prints raw market cap 116,049,092,437,500.0 and ADTV 427,113,583,150.8; fund record:174 says capex and EBITDA leave FCFF 38.6, which depends on a 131.9 NWC release not shown there; fund record:103 cites S3 for "nine-tenths" when S9 p19 gives 89.1%.
challenges.answer: Market cap and ADTV now formatted in Rp tn via the idrtn formatter; the FCFF bridge in §3 shows the working-capital release (NWC from 610.8 to 478.9, delta -131.9) rather than only the net FCFF; the mining share cites the audited segment note in S9.

challenges.challenge: The cross-guarantee bear case uses facility plafon Rp6.42tn (F63-F66) rather than outstanding balances, so the "full stack" overstates the contingent claim; the report does not state drawn amounts or maturity.
challenges.answer: §5 and §6 now state that the guarantee amounts are facility plafon, not drawn balances, that the accounts do not split drawn from undrawn, and that the bear tail uses the full maximum with the undrawn share disclosed as unknown rather than assumed away.

challenges.challenge: S19 and S20 carry obvious placeholder sha256 values (1f4e0b7a... and 2a3b4c5d...), and fund record is a 3,490-byte stub with no GEMS target or price, yet the DSSA mark of 1,116.60 depends on the GEMS 6,747.26 target.
challenges.answer: S20 is now the full GEMS report plus a resolved model snapshot (tp_final 6,747.26, FY2025A NP parent 258.23, equity, net debt), with the real SHA-256 registered; S19 was re-pointed to the archived IDX Channel article that its text actually is, and re-hashed. No placeholder hashes remain.

challenges.challenge: The model uses spot USD/IDR 18,128 while the sector deck's FY2027E benchmark is 18,350; for a USD-reporting issuer whose target is translated to rupiah, the choice moves the target and is not reconciled.
challenges.answer: §4 now discloses the FX choice: the model translates at spot while the house macro deck carries a slightly weaker FY2027E rate, the gap is about one per cent and moves tp_final one-for-one; it is disclosed rather than blended because the issuer earns in dollars.

missing_bull_case.note: The bull case is a mechanical -10pp discount (tp 267) with no dated catalyst and no credit for H1-2026 NP +79.6% or technology revenue +95.6% (S6). The GEMS FY2026 interim of USD200m paid 22 Oct 2026 (S20, GEMS F13), ~USD102m to DSSA, is not reflected in the upstream dividend line or post_bs_review.

response.note: Addressed in C10: dated GEMS final dividend (30 Jun 2027) and first DSSA distribution; data-centre project excluded with reason.

missing_bear_case.note: Bear only widens the holdco discount by 10pp (tp 200, -14%) and ignores the GEMS bear mark (51% x 2,303 = ~34% of the base stake, parent value -29%), a book haircut, the 29-Oct BSDE land sale, the 2 Nov 2026 HSC/IHSG exit, and the Rp6.42tn guarantee plafon. §6 says the BSDE/NCI searches found nothing, which is false on the record.
